summary: The narrator, reeling from the deaths of Anton and Penny, the information broker whose search was apparently traced, questions whether an old grudge or his own involvement caused the attack. He pressures his client Courtney, a frightened young woman on the run from a drug cartel, authorities, and a dirty cop, but she insists she doesn't know what the men at her place were looking for. The narrator is angry at her tears, and she responds with shock and guilt before he drives them into an alley toward a hideout called a bolt hole.
one_line: A fugitive-rescue narrator, shaken by the deaths of his broker and an associate, confronts his tearful client Courtney during a tense drive to a hideout.
key_facts: The narrator reasons that whoever targeted Anton had enough time to set up the attack once they caught onto Anton's search.
The narrator suspects that an old client with a grudge might have provoked the attack, though he doubts the attack was caused by what he had brought Anton.
The narrator says the job was supposed to be easy: rescue the kid, get her out of the country, and be home in time for dinner.
Two people sitting at a computer looking things up for the narrator died during the operation.
The narrator's client Courtney is hugging her knees, crying, with her ponytail hiding her face.
Courtney insists, "I don't—I don't know. I swear I don't" when asked what the men at her place were looking for.
The narrator lists Courtney's pursuers as a drug cartel that wants her dead, government men in dark suits, a dirty cop, and an unknown player willing to commit arson and murder.
The narrator has lost his information broker, and he thinks of Penny, a twelve-year-old hacker who was taught to pay her taxes on time.
Courtney cries softly in the passenger seat the whole way to the bolt hole the narrator drives them to.
The narrator tells Courtney, "For Christ's sake, you didn't even know them."
Courtney responds, "How can you be so cold?"
Courtney's horrified reaction to the narrator's question about guilt leads her to say, "This was about us? Oh, God—that was only this morning!"
The narrator slams the car into park in a grimy alleyway.
The narrator admits he isn't any good with people.
